name: Ukok Plateau
full: A high-mountain plateau in the far south of Kosh-Agach District, at the junction of the borders of Russia, Kazakhstan, China and Mongolia; entry from the village of Kosh-Agach via the border post near the village of Belyashi and the Teply Klyuch Pass (Dzhumalinsky springs). Most of it is the Ukok Quiet Zone nature park (part of the UNESCO site “Golden Mountains of Altai”).
near: The village of Belyashi (the last village before the border post and the Teply Klyuch Pass); the district centre, the village of Kosh-Agach, is ~140–150 km from the plateau (Altapress 2018, pikabu 2020); the village of Dzhazator — on the northwest side of the Teply Klyuch Pass.
elev: 2200–2500 m (plateau; bolshayastrana, geocaching.su); the main part of the park is above 2500 m (Directorate of Protected Areas of the Altai Republic); the Teply Klyuch Pass ~2400 m at the Dzhumalinsky springs (pikabu 2020) / 2600 m (make-trip) — the sources disagree; the highest point nearby is Kuyten-Uul (Nairamdal) 4374 m (welcometoaltai).
short: A treeless high-mountain plateau on the border of four countries: hundreds of lakes, the Tabyn-Bogdo-Ola glaciers, burial mounds of the Pazyryk culture (where the “Ukok Princess” was found in 1993), the radon Dzhumalinsky springs. SUV only, border zone, a season of about a month and a half.
desc: Ukok is a cold high-mountain steppe-tundra at an altitude of 2200–2500 m in the southwest corner of Kosh-Agach District, where the borders of Russia, Kazakhstan, China and Mongolia meet. Since 1998 part of the plateau has been the Ukok Quiet Zone nature park (252,904 ha, zones A/B/C; Directorate of Protected Areas of the Altai Republic), which is part of the UNESCO World Heritage site “Golden Mountains of Altai”. In the south the Tabyn-Bogdo-Ola range (Tavan-Bogdo-Ula) rises above the plateau with its glaciers and the peak of Kuyten-Uul (4374 m). The plateau has more than 800 lakes (bolshayastrana), the sources of the Ak-Alakha and Kalguty rivers, the Bertek tract with dozens of archaeological sites, petroglyphs, deer stones and balbals (stone figures); 150–180 monuments in all. In 1993, in the Ak-Alakha-3 burial mound, N. Polosmak found the mummy of a woman of the Pazyryk culture (5th–3rd centuries BC) — the “Ukok Princess” (now in the Anokhin National Museum in Gorno-Altaysk). Snow leopards, Altai argali (mountain sheep), golden eagles and Pallas's cats live here. The climate is sharply continental: in summer up to +25…+30 °C by day, frosts at night, and snow is possible in any month. The tourist season is effectively from mid-July to late August. There is no infrastructure: overnight stays are in tents or in tour operators' yurts, and the nearest cabins are at the Dzhumalinsky springs by the Teply Klyuch Pass. The plateau is in the border zone, and the way leads through the border post near Belyashi.
guide: Ukok is the end of the world in the literal sense: no trees, no people, only wind, lakes and the white wall of Tabyn-Bogdo-Ola on the horizon. For Altaians it is the “pasture of the heavens” and the land of the dead — after the “Ukok Princess” was taken to Novosibirsk in 1993, many linked earthquakes and misfortunes to it; don't take so much as a stone from here. Before the plateau, be sure to bathe in the radon Dzhumalinsky springs at Teply Klyuch (no longer than ~20 minutes). Look for deer stones and balbals in the Bertek tract on the plateau, and at Goose Lake (Gusinoye) watch the reflection of the glaciers. Travel only in a group of 2+ cars or with a local driver — help here is a hundred kilometres away.
see: The Ak-Alakha-3 burial mound (“Ukok Princess”, 49.2997, 87.5625); the Bertek tract (63 monuments of various eras, sib-guide), the Bertek rock-art site (100+ petroglyphs, bolshayastrana); deer stones and balbals; the Tabyn-Bogdo-Ola range with its glaciers and Kuyten-Uul peak 4374 m; Goose Lake (Gusinoye; Tashanta?) with a view of Tabyn-Bogdo-Ola; the Kaldzhin-Kul lakes and the Kaldzhinka waterfall (maral-travel); the “Gates of Ukok”; the Dzhumalinsky (Teply Klyuch) radon springs; on the way — the Tarkhata megalithic complex and the Kyzyl-Chin valley (“Mars”) near Chagan-Uzun.
skip: You are travelling in an ordinary passenger car, you have fewer than 5–6 free days, you aren't ready for nights in a tent in frosts, for no signal and no medical help for 100+ km — or you are a foreigner without a border-zone permit arranged in advance.
diff: High logistically: a prepared SUV, fords, rocky climbs to the Teply Klyuch Pass, altitude 2200–2600 m, no signal or services. Physically the hikes are easy to moderate (tour operators offer radial hikes to the glacier of up to ~20 km, vpoxod).
when: Mid-July to late August (Altapress: a season of ~1 month, late July — late August; bolshayastrana — “the second half of summer”); from September to June roads wash out/drift over and passes close.
hours: Round the clock; the Ukok Quiet Zone nature park (Directorate of Protected Areas of the Altai Republic) has no park checkpoint; passage through the border post near Belyashi (passport/permit check).
daytime: Early morning and evening — soft light on Tabyn-Bogdo-Ola and the lakes, less wind; by day strong winds and the weather changes several times a day.
how: The Chuysky Trakt (R256 highway) to the village of Kosh-Agach (≈890 km from Novosibirsk by the highway's kilometre markers; ~600 km from Gorno-Altaysk, ~700 km from Biysk — bolshayastrana). Then dirt road/steppe ~30 km to the border post near the village of Belyashi, another ~40 km to the fork (left — to the Teply Klyuch Pass and the Dzhumalinsky springs, right — Tarkhata), then a steep rocky climb to the pass and a descent onto the plateau. Kosh-Agach — Dzhumalinsky springs ~100–140 km, ~3–4 h (make-trip, pikabu 2020); Kosh-Agach — plateau ~150 km (Altapress). Only a prepared SUV/UAZ, preferably 2+ cars.
needcar: Yes — only an SUV (a UAZ, a Land Cruiser, the Severtrak all-terrain vehicles of tour operators). There is no public transport beyond Kosh-Agach.
self: Yes, for Russian citizens with a prepared SUV and off-road experience (passport; an FSB permit is for the 5-km border strip, and the Ak-Alakha-3 mound and the south of the plateau lie right by the Chinese border — better to get the permit in advance). For foreigners — only with a permit, processing ~30 days or more (tour operators close sales 3 weeks ahead — maral-travel; vpoxod — 2 months ahead for foreigners).
roadtype: The paved road ends at Kosh-Agach; then dirt and steppe tracks across the Chuya steppe to the post, then rocky tracks, fords (the Dzhumaly River and others), a steep climb to the Teply Klyuch Pass; on the plateau — tracks across tundra and boggy sections, “there are no roads, only directions”.
traveltime: Kosh-Agach — plateau ~2.5 h in a prepared SUV (akkem-tur.ru); Gorno-Altaysk — Kosh-Agach 1 day (~450–500 km, RussiaDiscovery: “450 km” along the highway on day 1); Kosh-Agach — Dzhumalinsky springs 3–4 h; the plateau — another 1–3 h depending on the spot. Tours: at least 5–6 days from Gorno-Altaysk.
stay: On the plateau — only tents or tour operators' yurt camps (RussiaDiscovery: 3 nights in yurts). The Dzhumalinsky springs — simple unheated cabins with bunks: 200 ₽/person, firewood 250 ₽/bundle, bathing 200 ₽/day (make-trip, year not specified). Kosh-Agach — the Rasul hotel (72a Novochuyskaya St.) from 4200 ₽ (101hotels, 2026); the district's tourist bases from 3700 ₽/night (tropki.ru, 2026).
net: There is no signal on the plateau (Altapress: “no signal or medical help within a 100 km radius”). The last reliable signal is Kosh-Agach/Belyashi; Dzhazator has gained mobile coverage (teletype 2022). You need a satellite tracker/phone.
entry: The Ukok Quiet Zone nature park is a regional protected area: from 01.07.2026 the visit fee for the Altai Republic's regional protected areas is 300 ₽ (it was 100), with the previous rate for residents of the Altai Republic (Tolk/Altapress 2026); according to akkem-tur.ru “the park pass is issued on the spot” (no price or year). The border-zone permit is free.
transfer: A private jeep trip — ~780,000 ₽ per car for 11 days (tomeet 2025); group tours 96,000–198,500 ₽/person for 6 days (2026). A one-off UAZ from Kosh-Agach to Ukok — price not found.
bring: Your passport (and the FSB permit if travelling to the border), fuel for 300+ km, spare wheels and tools, a tow rope, a warm sleeping bag (down to −5…−10 °C at night even in August — teletype 2022), a down jacket, windproof and waterproof clothing, a gas stove/primus (no firewood), water/a filter, a first-aid kit, sun protection (altitude), satellite communication, a paper/offline map, a tracker.
warn: Border zone (Kosh-Agach District; FSB order no. 282/2006 as amended by no. 512/2022): Russian citizens need a passport, with a check at the border post near Belyashi; in the 5-km strip along the border a permit is needed (Gosuslugi, the FSB Border Directorate for the Altai Republic in Gorno-Altaysk or its office in Kosh-Agach, 2 Armeyskaya St., +7 388-42 2-34-70); for foreigners a permit is mandatory everywhere. The fine for violating the regime is 500–1000 ₽ (Administrative Code, Altapress 2018). Solo trips are not recommended; fords, snow and frosts in summer; no medical help or signal for 100+ km; radon at the Dzhumalinsky springs — no more than ~20 min a day, consult a doctor if you have illnesses. Altitude 2200–2600 m. A sacred place for Altaians — don't touch the burial mounds and stones, excavations are prohibited. Ticks — lower down in the valleys (in the Altai Republic 3600 bites were reported by 25.08.2026).
food: In Kosh-Agach — Kazakh and Altai cuisine: beshbarmak, baursaks, tea with milk and salt (talkan), kurut; on the plateau — only your own food. No specific cafes were found.
reviews: No 2GIS/Yandex/Google ratings for the plateau were found. The Rasul hotel in Kosh-Agach is on TripAdvisor (reviews since 2014). Typical pros in the reports: “the end of the world”, solitude, glaciers, lakes, archaeology; cons: a hard road, cold, wind, no signal or infrastructure, high tour prices.

p.sum: Ukok is an expedition destination: the Chuysky Trakt to Kosh-Agach (1 day), then 3–4 h of off-road driving through the border post near Belyashi and the Teply Klyuch Pass (Dzhumalinsky springs) onto the plateau. 4×4 only, season from mid-July to August, nights in tents/yurts. The easiest way is a 6-day tour from 96,000 ₽.

p.budget.economy: On your own in your own 4×4 in a group of cars: fuel + food + 200 ₽ a night at Teply Klyuch — an estimate, there is no data on the full budget
p.permits: Russian citizens: a passport at the post; an FSB permit — for the 5-km strip (Gosuslugi, free, up to 15 days — Altapress; the FSB Border Directorate for the Altai Republic, Gorno-Altaysk, 94 Kommunistichesky Ave., +7 388-22 4-82-00; Kosh-Agach, 2 Armeyskaya St., +7 388-42 2-34-70). Foreigners — a permit is mandatory, apply 1–2 months ahead. Online registration with the Ministry of Emergency Situations. Protected area — a 300 ₽ fee is possible (regional protected areas since 01.07.2026).
p.access: Not suitable for older people and small children (altitude, cold, bumpy roads, no medical help); tours — from 15–16 years. Dogs — not recommended (quiet zone, wild animals).
